pathway.title: Anemia in Pregnancy — Classification and Treatment
pathway.scope: Outpatient prenatal care, from diagnosed anemia through postpartum handoff. Screening is upstream of this pathway.
pathway.target_population: Adult pregnant patients with diagnosed anemia; hemoglobinopathy disease, thalassemia syndromes, and CKD-associated anemia are detected and routed out.

condition_codes.usage: secondary trigger — often coded alongside O99.01x

properties.title: Empiric Oral Iron Trial (if chosen at DP-1; not with hemoglobinopathy disease)
properties.description: Branch-entry only, via DP-1 criterion 1a (empiric oral iron without iron studies). With no hemoglobinopathy disease on file (gate-empiric-no-hgbpathy) it opens Step 2.8, the iron-route choice (DP-3), so the empiric arm chooses between the oral trial and IV iron without an oral trial as ferritin-confirmed IDA does — except that IV iron first, with no ferritin on file, orders a ferritin, starts oral iron meanwhile and gives IV iron only once a ferritin < 30 ng/mL confirms iron deficiency. With sickle cell disease, a thalassemia syndrome or HbC/HbE disease on file, empiric iron is not given: gate-hgbpathy-microcytic opens Step 1.8 (iron studies) instead — choose confirmatory studies at DP-1 for the iron path. Numbered 1.5 so it sorts directly after Stage 1 with a number of its own.

properties.title: Oral Iron Trial (if chosen at DP-3)
properties.description: Branch-entry only, via DP-3 criterion 3a (no reason to skip the oral trial). Holds Steps 2.1–2.3 — oral iron, the trial period and the 2–4-week response check — on both arms (ferritin-confirmed IDA and empiric iron), since DP-3 is reached from both. Numbered 2.5 so it has a number of its own; its steps keep theirs.

properties.title: Oral Iron While IV Iron Waits (before 14 weeks, or until ferritin confirms iron deficiency)
properties.description: Branch-entry only, via gate-oral-bridge-ga on Step 2.9: IV iron without an oral trial was chosen at DP-3, but IV iron cannot be given yet — either no ferritin is on file (the empiric arm skips iron studies; Step 2.12 orders one, and IV iron waits for ferritin < 30 ng/mL), or it is before 14 0/7 weeks with iron deficiency confirmed. Holds the oral trial’s Steps 2.1–2.3 — oral iron, the trial period and the 2–4-week response check — so iron starts now. Once a ferritin < 30 is on file and the patient is 14 weeks or later, IV iron opens instead and this stage closes (DP-3 is asked again at each visit). With a ferritin of 30 or more on file it stays closed: no iron deficiency, no iron. Numbered 2.6 so it has a number of its own; its steps keep theirs.

properties.title: Microcytic anemia: iron strategy
properties.description: Entered only via gate-microcytic (MCV < 80 fL). Hosts DP-1: empiric oral iron vs confirmatory iron studies first. Normocytic and macrocytic anemia never reach this step; they go to Steps 1.3 / 1.4 through their own MCV gates. With hemoglobinopathy disease on file the empiric branch opens iron studies only (Step 1.8); the confirmatory branch leads to the same iron treatment as any confirmed iron deficiency.

properties.title: Hemoglobinopathy disease, empiric iron chosen: iron studies instead
properties.description: Entered only via gate-hgbpathy-microcytic on Stage 1.5: empiric oral iron was chosen at DP-1 for a patient with sickle cell disease, a thalassemia syndrome or HbC/HbE disease on file. Empiric iron is not given (gate-empiric-no-hgbpathy closes it). Confirm iron deficiency first: ferritin < 30 ng/mL confirms it; iron, TIBC and transferrin saturation help separate it from the hemoglobinopathy's own microcytosis. Iron for confirmed deficiency follows DP-1's confirmatory-studies branch (Step 1.2 → Stage 2), directed with hematology/MFM (Steps 3.1 / 3.2).

properties.title: Response assessment
properties.description: Hemoglobin recheck 2–4 weeks after starting oral iron. Read from the chart: responding = Hgb risen ≥ 1 g/dL since oral iron started, or Hgb at target (≥ 11 g/dL; ≥ 10.5 in the second trimester) → Step 2.4; not responding = risen < 1 g/dL and below target → Step 2.6. The rise is not judged before day 14 of oral iron: until then (and at the visit that starts it) neither branch opens and nothing is asked, unless Hgb is already at target.

properties.title: Nonresponse management
properties.description: Reached only when the Step 2.3 recheck shows no response to oral iron (hemoglobin rise < 1 g/dL at least 14 days after starting it, and below the trimester target). Hosts DP-2: expanded workup, and IV iron after the first trimester.

properties.title: Iron treatment route: oral trial or IV iron first
properties.description: Reached on both iron arms: ferritin-confirmed iron deficiency anemia (Stage 2) and empiric oral iron chosen at DP-1 (Stage 1.5). Hosts DP-3: an oral iron trial (the default), or IV iron without an oral trial for documented oral-iron intolerance, suspected malabsorption, or anemia diagnosed at 34 weeks or later.

properties.title: IV iron without an oral trial
properties.description: Chosen at DP-3. IV iron is given only after the first trimester (gestational age 14 0/7 weeks or later, gate-iv-iron-ga-direct → Step 2.13) and only once a ferritin < 30 ng/mL confirms iron deficiency (gate-ida-confirmed-iv → Step 2.10). On the confirmed arm that ferritin is already on file. On the empiric arm, which skips iron studies, a ferritin is ordered (gate-no-ferritin-on-file → Step 2.12) and oral iron starts meanwhile (gate-oral-bridge-ga → Stage 2.6); before 14 weeks oral iron is given until IV iron can be. DP-3 is asked again at each visit.

properties.title: Malabsorption on the chart: IV iron without an oral trial favoured (DP-3 criterion 3c)
properties.description: Entered only via gate-malabsorption-chart on Step 2.8 (both iron arms). The chart carries a condition that impairs oral iron absorption, which supports DP-3 criterion 3c. A recommendation shown next to the DP-3 question, not a decision: the route is still chosen at DP-3.

properties.title: No ferritin on file: order ferritin before IV iron
properties.description: Entered only via gate-no-ferritin-on-file on Step 2.9: IV iron without an oral trial was chosen at DP-3 with no ferritin in the last 90 days — the empiric arm, which skips iron studies. IV iron is given only once a ferritin < 30 ng/mL confirms iron deficiency (Step 2.13); oral iron starts meanwhile (Stage 2.6).

properties.title: IV iron first: ferritin must confirm iron deficiency
properties.description: Entered only via gate-iv-iron-ga-direct (gestational age 14 0/7 weeks or later) on Step 2.9. IV iron (Step 2.10) opens only through gate-ida-confirmed-iv — gate-ida-confirmed’s own condition, ferritin < 30 ng/mL within 90 days. On the confirmed arm the ferritin that opened Stage 2 satisfies it. On the empiric arm a missing ferritin is asked for and IV iron waits for it; a ferritin of 30 or more closes IV iron.

properties.title: Empiric iron vs confirmatory studies first

properties.description: No evidence of causes other than iron deficiency — empiric oral iron reasonable without iron studies. Not with hemoglobinopathy disease (sickle cell disease, thalassemia syndrome, HbC/HbE disease): with one on file this branch gives iron studies only; choose confirmatory studies first.
Atypical features, uncertain etiology, or confirmation preferred — ferritin/iron studies first
Intolerance or nonadherence despite coaching — consider IV iron
Suspected malabsorption (enteric-coated tablets, antacids, bariatric surgery, IBD) — consider IV iron
Suspected incorrect diagnosis or blood loss — expanded workup
Moderate–severe iron deficiency anemia within ~4–6 weeks of anticipated delivery, or oral failure near term — IV iron

properties.title: Oral iron trial vs IV iron without an oral trial

properties.description: No reason to skip the oral trial — start oral iron and recheck hemoglobin in 2–4 weeks
Documented intolerance of oral iron (e.g. on a prior course) — IV iron without an oral trial

Suspected malabsorption (bariatric surgery, inflammatory bowel disease, celiac disease, chronic antacid use) — IV iron without an oral trial. A malabsorption code on the chart opens Step 2.11 to recommend this criterion; the choice stays with the provider.

Anemia diagnosed at 34 weeks or later (iron deficiency confirmed, or presumed on the empiric arm) — too little time for an oral trial; IV iron (on the empiric arm, once a ferritin < 30 ng/mL confirms iron deficiency; oral iron meanwhile)

properties.title: Transfusion decliner
properties.prompt: Does the patient decline blood transfusion or specific blood products (e.g., for religious reasons)?

properties.name: Ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron)
properties.instructions: Avoid enteric-coated/sustained-release forms. Empty stomach preferred; small snack if GI upset. Separate from calcium/antacids/tea/coffee by ≥2 h. Vitamin C co-administration optional. Alternate-day dosing is an evidence-based tolerability option (non-pregnant trials; not a US pregnancy recommendation).

properties.name: Ferrous gluconate 300–324 mg (34–38 mg elemental)
properties.instructions: Lower elemental dose; gentler GI profile.

properties.name: Ferrous fumarate 324–325 mg (106 mg elemental)
properties.instructions: Highest elemental content per tablet.

properties.name: Iron sucrose (Venofer)
properties.instructions: Label indication is CKD — pregnancy use off-label. Multiple visits; historically most-used in pregnancy.
properties.dose: 200 mg IV per session × 5 within 14 days (~1,000 mg total)

properties.name: Ferric derisomaltose (Monoferric)
properties.instructions: Single-visit total replacement preferred. Hypophosphatemia 3.5%.
properties.dose: 1,000 mg IV single dose over ≥20 min (≥50 kg; 20 mg/kg if <50 kg)

properties.name: Ferric carboxymaltose (Injectafer)
properties.instructions: Symptomatic hypophosphatemia 2.1%; osteomalacia postmarketing — check phosphate on repeat courses.
properties.dose: 750 mg × 2 ≥7 days apart (total 1,500 mg), or single 15 mg/kg ≤1,000 mg

properties.name: Low-molecular-weight iron dextran (INFeD)
properties.instructions: BOXED WARNING: anaphylaxis. Mandatory 25 mg test dose. Single-visit total-dose infusion exceeds the 100 mg/day label — flag for local policy.

properties.name: Folic acid 1 mg
properties.instructions: For folate-deficiency macrocytic anemia (dominant macrocytic cause in US pregnancy).

properties.name: Cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) 1,000 mcg
properties.instructions: ACOG's regimen is specified for total gastrectomy; no general oral high-dose regimen in fetched sources.

properties.name: Docusate sodium 100 mg
properties.instructions: Non-conflicting adjunct — stool softener for iron-induced constipation.

properties.name: Enteric-coated / sustained-release iron preparations
properties.instructions: Dissolve poorly and may be less effective — do not use for repletion.

properties.name: Epoetin alfa
properties.instructions: Restricted context: transfusion-decliner optimization with parenteral iron. Not recommended for routine anemia.

27 mg/day iron requirement in pregnancy. Heme sources: lean beef, turkey, chicken, shrimp, clams, oysters; liver occasionally. Non-heme sources: fortified cereals, white and kidney beans, lentils, peas, spinach, nuts, raisins. Pair plant iron with vitamin C (orange juice, grapefruit, strawberries, tomatoes, peppers, broccoli) or with meat in the same meal.

Coffee, tea, dairy and calcium, soy, and antacids reduce iron absorption. Keep them about 2 hours away from iron-focused meals and from the iron tablet. Take calcium supplements at a different time of day.

Plant iron is absorbed at roughly 5–12% versus 14–18% from a mixed diet. Build meals around an iron source paired with vitamin C. Take the prenatal vitamin daily. Tell the care team about a plant-based diet so lab surveillance can be closer.

Morning empty-stomach dosing with orange juice or another vitamin C source; add a small snack if GI upset. Keep the 2-hour separation rules. Dark stools are normal. Plan for constipation, including docusate if needed. Alternate-day dosing is an option to discuss. Expect the response to take weeks — keep the scheduled lab recheck.

properties.topic: When to call us right away
properties.instructions: Review the urgent maternal warning signs (CDC Hear Her / AIM) with the patient and give her the handout; she should seek care immediately for any of them, and always say that she is pregnant (source: https://www.cdc.gov/hearher/maternal-warning-signs/index.html). Also ask whether she craves or eats non-food items (ice, clay, dirt, starch, paper, paint chips); this is common, so ask without judgement.

properties.topic: Malabsorption on the chart: consider IV iron first
properties.instructions: The problem list carries a condition that reduces oral iron absorption (bariatric surgery, Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, celiac disease, short bowel syndrome or intestinal failure, postsurgical or unspecified intestinal malabsorption, or gastrectomy). This supports choosing IV iron without an oral trial at DP-3 (criterion 3c), most strongly after a malabsorptive bariatric procedure (e.g. Roux-en-Y gastric bypass) or with active inflammatory bowel disease; with quiescent IBD or a restrictive procedure an oral trial remains reasonable. IV iron is given from 14 0/7 weeks, and only once a ferritin < 30 ng/mL confirms iron deficiency; until then (before 14 weeks, or on the empiric arm while its ferritin is outstanding), choosing IV first starts oral iron.

properties.name: Timely treatment-response assessment
properties.measure: Numerator: patients started on iron therapy with a hemoglobin recheck resulted within 6 weeks of initiation. Denominator: patients started on iron therapy in this pathway.

properties.name: Hemorrhage risk assessment with anemia input
properties.measure: Birth admissions with a completed hemorrhage risk assessment, in which anemia is a scored factor (AIM HEM P3).
